extracted.intended_audience: Machine learning researchers, authors, reviewers, and action editors interested in submitting to or participating in Transactions on Machine Learning Research (TMLR)
extracted.subtask_description: Announcement and policy summary for submitting to the Transactions on Machine Learning Research (TMLR), including submission capacity rules, reviewer/AE assignment quotas, and the criteria for various paper certifications. Intended to guide authors, reviewers, and action editors on expectations and procedures for participation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow submission guidelines and templates
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors must follow the TMLR submission guidelines and use the updated LaTeX templates provided on the TMLR website and submit via the tested OpenReview site.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The announcement states the website has submission guidelines and updated LaTeX templates and that the OpenReview site is tested and ready; authors should consult those resources before submitting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monthly submission capacity and possible temporary stop
rubrics_metrics.description: TMLR can handle only about 150 submissions per month given current AE and reviewer capacity; if this capacity is exceeded, TMLR will stop accepting submissions temporarily.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because there are strict quotas on how many papers may be assigned to any AE or reviewer, exceeding capacity would lead to longer review turnarounds or higher quotas, which TMLR has decided is not acceptable; authors should expect possible temporary submission stoppages if capacity is reached.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strict assignment quotas per Action Editor and reviewer
rubrics_metrics.description: There are strict quotas on how many papers may be assigned to any Action Editor (AE) or reviewer to limit workload and maintain fair review practices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The quotas are intended to prevent overloading AEs/reviewers; the announcement emphasizes maintaining reasonable per-person assignment limits rather than raising quotas to handle excess submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monitoring and possible individual submission limits for prolific authors
rubrics_metrics.description: TMLR will closely monitor authors with high numbers of submissions and may impose individual limits to maintain fair access for all authors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a fairness policy: if necessary, individual limits will be imposed to ensure equitable access to review resources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Soliciting to review a submission must be approved by the Action Editor
rubrics_metrics.description: If you were not invited to be a reviewer (or were invited but couldn’t accept), you are welcome to contribute and solicit to review a submission, but this is subject to approval by the Action Editor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors and community members can volunteer to review papers in their area of expertise; final assignment and approval rest with the AE handling the submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Survey certification — criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Survey certifications are awarded for papers that include exceptionally thorough or insightful surveys of literature and methods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Surveys should provide exceptional thoroughness or insight into literature and methods to qualify; this certification signals high-quality survey work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reproducibility certification — criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Reproducibility certifications are awarded for papers that go beyond simple verification of a previous result and contribute valuable analyses or additional experiments which provide new insights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To earn this certification, submissions should do more than replicate prior results: they should add analyses or experiments that deepen understanding or reveal new findings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Featured certification — criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Featured certifications are awarded to high quality papers selected by the Action Editor, roughly equivalent to choosing a paper for an oral/spotlight at a top-tier conference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an AE-level selection recognizing particularly strong papers; selection criteria are AE-driven and analogous to spotlight/oral choices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Outstanding certification — criteria and cadence
rubrics_metrics.description: Outstanding certification is awarded by the Editors-in-Chief approximately on an annual basis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a top-level recognition awarded by EICs; timing is roughly annual and selection is by the EICs rather than AEs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expert Reviewer certification — criteria and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Expert Reviewer certification will be awarded to papers authored by very highly rated reviewers, but implementation requires sufficient evidence and so will wait until TMLR has enough data to identify those expert reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This certification links author recognition to reviewer quality metrics; it will be introduced only after TMLR has accumulated evidence to identify highly rated reviewers reliably.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuous online publication (no annual issues/proceedings)
rubrics_metrics.description: TMLR will not have annual issues or proceedings; it is entirely online and publishes continuously.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because there are no proceedings, readers and authors are advised to follow the mailing list digest (daily or weekly) or Twitter feeds for announcements of new submissions, accepted papers, and certifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exploration of non-PDF, interactive submission formats
rubrics_metrics.description: TMLR is considering supporting non-PDF, interactive submissions in the future and has set up an internal committee to explore options and make recommendations adapted to TMLR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should be aware that TMLR is open to format innovation beyond traditional PDFs; details and policies will depend on committee recommendations and future announcements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use the FAQ and contact TMLR for issues or feedback
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors, reviewers, and Action Editors should check the FAQ regularly and contact TMLR if they encounter issues or have feedback on the journal or review process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This procedural guidance encourages community members to consult the FAQ for role-specific information and to report problems or provide feedback to help smooth launch issues.
